//: npm, and do not change it to bun without proving it on a deployment.
This was switched to bun once and every deployment failed from that
commit until it was switched back. Vercel builds npm here perfectly well
-- it had been doing so all along -- and the failure it was meant to fix
was never Vercel's: `npm install` crashes on THIS machine with npm 10
('Cannot read properties of null (reading edgesOut)') while resolving
vitest's peer dependencies. Locally, use bun. Vercel uses npm.
The cost of that is real and worth knowing: there is no
package-lock.json, and there cannot be one until npm can resolve the tree
locally, so Vercel resolves dependencies fresh on every build. A bad
release of any transitive dependency can therefore break a build without
anything here changing. If that ever happens, the symptom is a build that
fails while the site keeps serving the last good one.
Whoever fixes that properly: get a working package-lock.json committed.
